decisions.reason: Because this water phantom is strategically relevant to the firm's particle-therapy dosimetry niche and has already survived the uncertain rollout stage, management would likely keep it unless its limited market falls clearly below aspiration levels.
As the surviving small-volume chamber after earlier portfolio pruning, it is close to the firm's core measurement business and would likely be retained while continuing to earn acceptable results.

A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models sits at the center of the firm's established offering, so its performance is likely at or above aspiration and unlikely to trigger withdrawal.
This relative-dosimetry chamber serves a narrower use case and therefore carries some review risk, but the firm would probably keep it while portfolio slack allows support for specialist customers.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional core-adjacent product for radiotherapy QA, making continued retention more likely than resource reallocation.
